messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 ALERT  hosted-runtime eu-west-1 reporting repeated OOMs in KV cache; autoscaler flapping and ~8% 5xx on generation routes. Paging on-call.

Alex: acknowledged. Pulling logs/metrics now. Which node pools impacted?

Jia: eu-west-1a, eu-west-1b primary. kvcache.entries per-pod shot up to >1.8M and resident memory at 95%. Continuous-batching + prefix caching appears to be retaining huge KV state for certain requests.

Sam (oncall-sre): grabbing top offenders and traffic traces. Running: `kubectl -n prod exec -it svc/metrics -- curl -s /query?m=kv_entries_per_pod|sort -nr | head`

Jia: logs show repeated requests with context_length values: 412k, 398k, 375k tokens. Those sessions are sticking around due to prefetch + batch dedupe semantics.

Alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable prefetch/pinning on hosted runtime, 2) hard cap kv entries per-session, 3) deploy batch_max_tokens reduction to cut in-flight context expansion, 4) add temporary token-length reject for >120k tokens. Who can push hotfix?

Jia: I can. Will roll to a single canary pool then expand. Patch diff I'm applying now:
```
# hotfix
runtime.kv_cache.max_entries_per_session = 60000
runtime.kv_cache.per_pod_hard_cap = 2000000
runtime.prefetch.enabled = false
runtime.batch.batch_max_tokens = 1536
runtime.request.max_context_tokens_hosted = 120000
```

Jia: kicking deploy to eu-west-1a canary. deploy-bot: start deploy-4047-hotfix at 2026-03-15T09:58:40Z

deploy-bot: canary deploy started by jia. ID deploy-4047-hotfix.

Sam: while canary rolls, I'm throttling inbound batch admission on the busiest frontends to reduce amplification. Applied temporary rate limit to 60rps for generation-prod routes.

Maria: support telemetry: ~42 customers saw elevated 5xx, 6 customers had >2m failed requests. Notifying top impacted customers now.

Jia: canary looks stable after 90s: memory droppped ~40% on that pod, kv entries back to ~30k. Rolling to rest of eu-west-1.

Alex: monitoring errors: `metrics query: 5xx_rate region=eu-west-1 window=5m` shows 5xx down from 8.2% -> 1.7% since canary. Good.

Priya (oncall-day): taking notes. Any sign of leak or is this purely cache growth from request sizes?

Jia: growth is request-driven. Continuous-batching dedupe behavior appended new keys when long prefix matched across batched requests; we didn't evict because prefix matching prevented per-request isolation. Will open PR to change dedupe to allocate per-session budgets.

Alex: immediate customer-facing action: put advisory on status page recommending prompt chunking and temporary limits. Maria please coordinate.

Maria: Drafted status update: short note explaining transient errors and the temporary 120k token limit on hosted tier; recommending chunked requests and contacting support for high-volume long-context use-cases. Will post in 10m.

Sam: Found 4 API keys responsible for ~75% of KV growth. Temporarily removed prefetch entitlement and flagged their accounts for outreach.

Jia: also enabled a per-pod absolute hard cap (2M entries) so a runaway cannot cause node OOM. If cap reached we will start returning 413-like error with structured guidance.

Alex: add monitoring alert to catch per-pod kv_entries > 1.5M again and trigger paged escalation.

Jia: pushing the token-length reject now; behaviour: for hosted requests >120k tokens respond with 413 + `please chunk context` and a link to docs. Rate-limited to avoid account grief. Deploying in 2m.

deploy-bot: rollout complete across eu-west-1 at 2026-03-15T10:23:01Z. ID deploy-4047-hotfix.

Alex: current status: 5xx baseline restored to ~0.7%, latency increase of ~30% for long-but-allowed requests, memory stable. Hotfix in place, customer comms drafted.

Maria: Customers updated; two large accounts asked for temporary Dedicated capacity — handoff to sales/solutions.

Priya: action items captured for postmortem: permanent fix for continuous-batching dedupe semantics, per-request KV budgets, eval harness for synthetic long-contexts, and an API quota/validation for hosted tier.

Jia: opening linked PRs and scheduling follow-up with eng-runtime + eng-ml to implement model-side safeguards (streamed context trimming).

incident-bot: Incident logged INC-2026-0315-007 severity=2 start=2026-03-15T09:58:21Z owner=Alex link=https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-0315-007

Alex: handing over to day shift. Priya, Sam and Maria you have the follow-ups. If any regression occurs re-page immediately. Thanks all.
